unstructured_evidence.text: Wallet-method transactions failed at a substantially higher rate for most of the business day on Aug 15, spanning every issuing bank and city in the dataset. Failures were dominated by gateway-side errors and risk-engine declines rather than bank timeouts, suggesting the issue sat with the wallet payment gateway itself rather than any specific bank or region.
unstructured_evidence.title: Elevated wallet payment failures across all issuing banks

unstructured_evidence.text: The wallet payment gateway partner's public status history shows a period of degraded performance for authorization requests on Aug 15, described by the partner as intermittent elevated error rates during a backend deployment window.
unstructured_evidence.title: Wallet gateway partner status note

unstructured_evidence.text: A retry-and-notify campaign for wallet transactions that failed on Aug 15 recovered approximately 40% of affected revenue within 48 hours. Recovery rates were noticeably lower than typical bank-timeout retry campaigns, consistent with a larger share of the failures being risk declines rather than transient errors.
unstructured_evidence.title: Wallet failure recovery campaign outcome

unstructured_evidence.text: A promotional flash sale on Aug 22 drove roughly triple the normal transaction volume for a four-hour window. Failure rates during the spike stayed in line with the recent baseline across every payment method, bank, and city checked; nothing in the failure data distinguished this period from an ordinary high-traffic evening.
unstructured_evidence.title: Volume spike during promotional flash sale, no degradation observed

unstructured_evidence.text: In mid-June, wallet top-ups linked to Axis Bank accounts experienced processing delays over a single afternoon, resolved within a few hours. This incident predates the current reporting window and involved wallet top-ups specifically, not wallet checkout payments.
unstructured_evidence.title: Historical: Axis Bank wallet top-up delays (unrelated period)

unstructured_evidence.text: Between 13:00 and 18:00 UTC on Aug 12, UPI transactions routed through HDFC Bank showed a sharp rise in failed authorizations, predominantly timing out at the bank's end. Transactions through other issuing banks over the same window were unaffected. The pattern was isolated to the HDFC UPI routing path specifically, not UPI as a whole.
unstructured_evidence.title: UPI failures concentrated on HDFC Bank routing

unstructured_evidence.text: For roughly two hours on the evening of Aug 17, processing latency rose across every payment method and every issuing bank simultaneously, with a corresponding increase in timeout-driven failures. No single method, bank, or city stood out individually; the pattern was uniform across the board, consistent with a shared upstream dependency rather than a bank- or method-specific problem.
unstructured_evidence.title: Broad processing latency increase, all payment methods

unstructured_evidence.text: Support ticket volume for 'payment failed' complaints roughly tripled in the early afternoon of Aug 12. Nearly all tickets we sampled mentioned UPI as the payment method, and where the customer's bank was mentioned, HDFC came up disproportionately often compared to a normal day.
unstructured_evidence.title: Support queue spike, UPI checkout failures

unstructured_evidence.text: A retry notification was sent to customers whose UPI payment through HDFC failed during the Aug 12 window. Of the transactions retried within 24 hours, roughly 55% completed successfully on a second attempt, mostly using the same UPI handle.
unstructured_evidence.title: Retry campaign results for Aug 12 HDFC UPI failures

unstructured_evidence.text: The UPI switch partner's incident notes for Aug 12 reference elevated timeout responses specifically attributed to one issuing bank's authorization servers during the early-to-mid afternoon, consistent with a bank-side rather than switch-side bottleneck.
unstructured_evidence.title: UPI switch partner note on bank-side timeouts
